name: Golden Retriever
visual_anchor: A fluffy golden retriever puppy sitting on green grass with its tongue out and a red ball at its paws, soft afternoon sunlight, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Friendly medium-large dog with a thick golden coat
Loves fetching balls and splashing in water
Often trained as a guide dog or therapy dog
First bred in the Scottish Highlands in the 1800s

facts_and_myths.claim: Golden retrievers have water-repellent fur.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their thick outer coat sheds water, which helped them fetch from lakes and rivers.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A golden retriever named Augie once held five tennis balls in its mouth at the same time.

facts_and_myths.claim: Golden retrievers make fierce guard dogs that scare away strangers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Golden retrievers are so friendly that they usually greet strangers with a wagging tail.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Their soft mouth can carry an egg without cracking it.

name: Labrador Retriever
visual_anchor: A happy chocolate-brown Labrador retriever splashing out of a sparkling blue lake with a stick in its mouth, bright sunny day, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Popular family dog with a short, thick coat
Comes in black, yellow or chocolate colors
Has a thick 'otter tail' and webbed toes for swimming
Its ancestors came from Newfoundland in Canada

facts_and_myths.claim: Labradors have webbed toes that help them swim.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Skin between their toes works like a paddle, making Labs strong, happy swimmers.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: For over 30 years in a row, Labs were the most registered dog breed in America.

facts_and_myths.claim: Chocolate Labs and yellow Labs are different dog breeds.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They are the same breed. Black, yellow and chocolate are just different coat colors.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A Lab's thick tail works like a boat rudder to help it steer while swimming.

name: German Shepherd
visual_anchor: A proud black-and-tan German shepherd with tall pointy ears sitting alertly on a grassy hill under a clear blue sky, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Large, smart dog with a black and tan coat
Has tall, pointy ears that stand straight up
Often works with police and search-and-rescue teams
First bred in Germany in 1899 to herd sheep

facts_and_myths.claim: German shepherds often help police and rescue teams.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their sharp noses, smarts and focus make them great at finding lost people and sniffing out clues.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Buddy, the first guide dog trained in America, was a German shepherd.

facts_and_myths.claim: German shepherds were first bred to be police dogs.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They were first bred to herd and protect sheep on German farms, which is how they got their name.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A German shepherd named Rin Tin Tin became a famous movie star in the 1920s.

name: Dalmatian
visual_anchor: A playful white Dalmatian covered in black spots running beside a shiny red fire truck on a sunny street, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: White dog covered in black or brown spots
Stars in the movie 101 Dalmatians
A classic mascot of firehouses
Once ran beside horse-drawn carriages and fire wagons

facts_and_myths.claim: Dalmatian puppies are born completely white.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their spots start to appear when they are about two weeks old and keep filling in as they grow.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Dalmatians can even have spots inside their mouths.

facts_and_myths.claim: Every Dalmatian has exactly the same spot pattern.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Each Dalmatian's spots are different, so no two dogs look exactly alike.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Dalmatians once ran ahead of horse-drawn fire wagons to help clear the way.

name: Poodle
visual_anchor: An elegant white standard poodle with a fluffy curly coat prancing across a flower garden full of pink blossoms, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Dog with a thick, curly, fluffy coat
Comes in toy, miniature and standard sizes
Famous for fancy pom-pom haircuts at dog shows
First bred in Germany to fetch ducks from water

facts_and_myths.claim: Poodles were first bred to fetch things from water.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Poodles are excellent swimmers, and their name comes from an old German word for splashing.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Poodles are often ranked the second smartest dog breed, right after Border Collies.

facts_and_myths.claim: Poodles were first bred in France.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Poodles were developed in Germany, even though they later became hugely popular in France.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Even though poodles came from Germany, the poodle is the national dog of France.

name: Beagle
visual_anchor: A cheerful tri-color beagle with long floppy ears sniffing colorful autumn leaves in a park, tail held high, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small hound with long floppy ears and a white-tipped tail
Usually has a brown, black and white coat
Has an amazing nose and loves to follow scents
Snoopy from the Peanuts comics is one

facts_and_myths.claim: Some beagles work at airports sniffing luggage.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their super noses help officers find fruits, plants and foods that should not be brought into a country.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In America, this team of airport sniffer dogs is called the Beagle Brigade.

facts_and_myths.claim: Beagles are quiet dogs that hardly make any noise.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Beagles are famous for loud barks and a long howl called baying.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Snoopy, the famous cartoon dog from Peanuts, is a beagle.

name: Chihuahua
visual_anchor: A tiny tan Chihuahua with huge pointy ears and big shiny eyes peeking out of a cozy pink blanket on a sofa, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Tiny dog that can fit in a handbag
Has very big ears and large round eyes
Often called the smallest dog breed in the world
Named after a state in Mexico

facts_and_myths.claim: The Chihuahua is named after a place in Mexico.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The breed takes its name from the Mexican state of Chihuahua.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some Chihuahua puppies are born with a soft spot on top of their head, like human babies.

facts_and_myths.claim: Tiny dogs like Chihuahuas do not need walks.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Even tiny dogs need daily walks and playtime to stay healthy and happy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Chihuahuas often love burrowing under blankets to stay cozy.

name: Pembroke Welsh Corgi
visual_anchor: A smiling orange-and-white corgi with short stubby legs and big upright ears trotting across a green meadow, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Low dog with very short legs and a long body
Has a fox-like face and big upright ears
Was a favorite pet of Queen Elizabeth II
Bred in Wales to herd cattle

facts_and_myths.claim: Queen Elizabeth II owned more than 30 corgis.
facts_and_myths.explanation: She loved Pembroke corgis and kept them throughout her long reign.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The word corgi is often said to mean 'dwarf dog' in Welsh.

facts_and_myths.claim: Corgis' short legs make them useless for farm work.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Corgis were skilled cattle herders, and being low helped them duck under kicking hooves.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Corgis herded cattle by gently nipping at their heels to keep them moving.

name: Siberian Husky
visual_anchor: A fluffy gray-and-white Siberian husky with bright blue eyes pulling a small sled through sparkling snow, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Fluffy, wolf-like dog that loves snow
Often has striking blue eyes
Famous for pulling sleds in teams
First bred by the Chukchi people of Siberia

facts_and_myths.claim: Some huskies have one blue eye and one brown eye.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Huskies often have eyes of two different colors. It is natural and does not affect their sight.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Husky sled teams helped carry medicine to Nome, Alaska, in 1925.

facts_and_myths.claim: Siberian huskies are part wolf.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Huskies only look wolf-like. They are fully domestic dogs bred to pull sleds.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Huskies often 'talk' with howls and woo-woo sounds instead of barking much.

name: Bulldog
visual_anchor: A chubby white-and-fawn bulldog with a wrinkly face lying happily on a soft green cushion in a sunny living room, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Stocky dog with a wrinkly face
Has a short, pushed-in nose and droopy cheeks
Often snores loudly while napping
A popular mascot for sports teams and universities

facts_and_myths.claim: Most bulldogs are not good swimmers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their heavy chest and short legs make swimming hard, so they need a dog life jacket near water.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Yale University's mascot, Handsome Dan, is a bulldog.

facts_and_myths.claim: Bulldogs are grumpy because they look grumpy.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Despite their frowning faces, bulldogs are usually gentle, calm and very loving.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Bulldogs often snore loudly because of their short, flat noses.

name: Shiba Inu
visual_anchor: A fox-like red-orange Shiba Inu with a curly tail standing on a wooden path under pink cherry blossoms, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small dog that looks a lot like a fox
Has a tail that curls up over its back
Known for its very independent, cat-like attitude
One of the oldest dog breeds from Japan

facts_and_myths.claim: The Shiba Inu is one of Japan's oldest dog breeds.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Shibas have lived in Japan's mountains for a very long time and were once used to flush birds from bushes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The famous 'Doge' meme shows a Shiba Inu named Kabosu.

facts_and_myths.claim: Shiba Inus are just baby Akitas.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They look alike, but the Shiba Inu is its own separate, smaller breed.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: When upset, Shibas can make a loud, dramatic noise nicknamed the 'Shiba scream'.

name: Pug
visual_anchor: A cute fawn pug with a black wrinkly face and curly tail tilting its head on a cozy rug next to a toy, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small dog with a wrinkly, squashed face
Has a black face mask and a curly tail
Makes funny snorting and snuffling sounds
Was a favorite pet of ancient Chinese emperors

facts_and_myths.claim: Pugs first came from ancient China.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Pugs were treasured by Chinese emperors long ago, then later became popular in Europe.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A group of pugs is sometimes jokingly called a 'grumble'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Pugs are great at running long distances in hot weather.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their flat faces make breathing hard in heat, so pugs need short walks and shady rest.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pugs were once a favorite pet of the Dutch royal family.

name: Dachshund
visual_anchor: A long, low red-brown dachshund with short legs and floppy ears trotting happily along a garden path, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Dog with a very long body and tiny short legs
Nicknamed after a long, skinny food
Comes in smooth, long-haired and wire-haired coats
Bred in Germany to dig into badger burrows

facts_and_myths.claim: The name Dachshund means 'badger dog' in German.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They were bred to wiggle into badger tunnels thanks to their long, low bodies.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A dachshund named Waldi was the first official Olympic mascot, in 1972.

facts_and_myths.claim: Dachshunds should be lifted carefully, supporting their long backs.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their long backs can get hurt easily, so support the chest and back end. Ask an adult to help.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Dachshunds have a surprisingly loud bark for such a small dog.

name: Persian Cat
visual_anchor: A fluffy white Persian cat with a flat face and big copper eyes lounging on a velvet purple cushion, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Cat with a very long, fluffy coat
Has a round, flat face and a short nose
Calm and quiet, loves lounging on cushions
Named after the old name of Iran

facts_and_myths.claim: Persian cats need their long fur brushed every day.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their thick, long coat tangles easily, so daily brushing keeps it smooth and knot-free.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Persian cats are named after Persia, the old name for Iran.

facts_and_myths.claim: Long-haired cats like Persians never shed.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Persians shed a lot of fur, especially as seasons change.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Persians are known as one of the calmest, quietest cat breeds.

name: Siamese Cat
visual_anchor: A sleek cream-colored Siamese cat with dark brown ears, face and paws and bright blue eyes sitting on a sunny windowsill, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Slim cat with a cream-colored body
Has darker ears, face, paws and tail
Has bright blue eyes and loves to 'talk' loudly
Comes from Thailand, once called Siam

facts_and_myths.claim: Siamese kittens are born almost completely white.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their darker points appear as they grow, on the cooler parts of the body like ears and paws.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Body heat keeps a Siamese cat's middle light, while cooler ears and paws turn darker.

facts_and_myths.claim: Siamese cats are very quiet and rarely meow.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Siamese cats are famous chatterboxes that meow loudly to get attention.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Siam is the old name for Thailand, where these cats come from.

name: Maine Coon
visual_anchor: A huge fluffy brown tabby Maine Coon cat with tufted ears and a bushy tail sitting on a snowy wooden porch, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Very large, shaggy pet cat
Has tufted ears and a big, bushy tail
Has wide paws that work like snowshoes
The official state cat of Maine in the USA

facts_and_myths.claim: Maine Coons are one of the largest pet cat breeds.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Maine Coons are much bigger than most house cats and grow slowly for several years.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Maine Coon is the official state cat of Maine.

facts_and_myths.claim: Maine Coons are part raccoon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cats and raccoons cannot have babies together. The bushy tail just looks raccoon-like.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Many Maine Coons enjoy playing with water, unlike most cats.

name: British Shorthair
visual_anchor: A round-faced, chubby blue-gray British Shorthair cat with big copper eyes sitting on a cozy knitted blanket, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Sturdy cat with a round, chubby face
Has a thick, plush coat like a teddy bear
Most famous in a blue-gray color with copper eyes
One of the oldest cat breeds from Britain

facts_and_myths.claim: The most famous British Shorthair color is a blue-gray.
facts_and_myths.explanation: This soft gray color is so well known that the breed is often called the British Blue.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Their dense coat feels like soft plush, which is why they look like teddy bears.

facts_and_myths.claim: All British Shorthairs are blue-gray.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They also come in black, white, cream, cinnamon and many other colors and patterns.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: British Shorthairs are known for being calm cats that enjoy staying on the ground.

name: Ragdoll Cat
visual_anchor: A big fluffy cream-and-brown Ragdoll cat with bright blue eyes relaxing in a child's gentle arms in a sunny room, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Large, fluffy cat with bright blue eyes
Has a light body with darker ears, face and tail
Often goes floppy and relaxed when picked up
Developed in California in the 1960s

facts_and_myths.claim: Ragdoll cats often go floppy when someone picks them up.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They relax like a soft toy, which is how the breed got its name.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ragdolls are sometimes called 'puppy cats' because they follow their people around.

facts_and_myths.claim: Ragdoll kittens are born with their full adult colors.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ragdoll kittens are born mostly white, and their colors slowly darken as they grow.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ragdolls can take three to four years to become fully grown.

name: Hamster
visual_anchor: A chubby golden hamster with puffed-out cheeks full of seeds sitting in soft wood shavings beside a little wheel, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small, round, fluffy pet rodent
Runs on a wheel, often at night
Stuffs food into stretchy cheek pouches
Syrian ones prefer to live alone in their cage

facts_and_myths.claim: Hamsters carry food in stretchy pouches inside their cheeks.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They fill their cheeks with food, then carry it to a hidden spot to store for later.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The word hamster comes from a German word meaning 'to hoard'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Hamsters are most active during the daytime.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Hamsters mostly sleep in the day and wake up to play in the evening and night.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A hamster's front teeth never stop growing, so it needs safe things to chew.

name: Guinea Pig
visual_anchor: A round brown-and-white guinea pig with a tuft of fur munching a green lettuce leaf on a bed of fresh hay, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Chubby pet rodent with no tail
Makes squeaky 'wheek wheek' sounds
Needs fresh veggies with vitamin C every day
First kept as pets in the Andes of South America

facts_and_myths.claim: Guinea pigs need vitamin C from their food every day.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Like people, their bodies cannot make vitamin C, so they need veggies like bell peppers.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Happy guinea pigs sometimes jump and twist in the air, which is called popcorning.

facts_and_myths.claim: Guinea pigs are a kind of pig from Guinea.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Guinea pigs are rodents, not pigs, and they come from South America, not Guinea.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Guinea pigs often squeal 'wheek' when they hear the fridge open, hoping for treats.

name: Pet Rabbit
visual_anchor: A fluffy white pet rabbit with long pink-lined ears nibbling hay on a soft blanket beside a small wooden hutch, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Fluffy pet with long ears and a cotton tail
Hops around and twitches its nose
Munches mostly on hay all day
Thumps its back feet to warn of danger

facts_and_myths.claim: A rabbit's teeth keep growing its whole life.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Chewing lots of hay wears their teeth down and keeps them the right length.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Happy rabbits sometimes leap and twist in the air, a move called a binky.

facts_and_myths.claim: Rabbits should mostly eat carrots.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Rabbits should mostly eat hay. Carrots are sugary, so they are only an occasional treat.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Rabbits thump their back feet loudly to warn other rabbits.

name: Goldfish
visual_anchor: A bright orange goldfish with flowing fins swimming among green plants and smooth pebbles in a clean, sparkling aquarium, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Shiny orange pet fish
Often kept in tanks and garden ponds
A small cousin of the carp
First kept as pets in ancient China

facts_and_myths.claim: Goldfish were first kept as pets in ancient China.
facts_and_myths.explanation: People in China bred wild carp for their gold color over a thousand years ago.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: With good care, pet goldfish can live for more than ten years.

facts_and_myths.claim: Goldfish only have a three-second memory.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Goldfish can remember things for months and can even learn to recognize feeding times.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Goldfish can be trained to swim toward a sound when it is time to eat.

name: Betta Fish
visual_anchor: A dazzling blue-and-red betta fish with long flowing fins gliding past green plants in a clear, glowing aquarium, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small fish with long, flowing, colorful fins
Males build floating nests out of bubbles
Can gulp air from the surface of the water
Comes from shallow rice paddies in Thailand

facts_and_myths.claim: Betta fish can breathe air from the water's surface.
facts_and_myths.explanation: A special organ lets them gulp air, which helped them live in shallow, still water.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Male bettas build floating nests made of tiny bubbles.

facts_and_myths.claim: Bettas are happiest living in a tiny bowl or vase.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Bettas need a heated tank with clean, filtered water to stay healthy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Two male bettas should never share a tank because they do not get along.

name: Red-Eared Slider
visual_anchor: A green red-eared slider turtle basking on a sunny rock beside clear water, with a bright red stripe behind its eye, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Popular pet turtle with a green shell
Loves sunbathing on rocks and logs
Has a red stripe behind each eye
Comes from rivers and ponds of the southern United States

facts_and_myths.claim: Red-eared sliders get their name from red patches near their ears.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They have a red stripe behind each eye and quickly slide off rocks into water.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: With good care, red-eared sliders can live for more than 20 years.

facts_and_myths.claim: A pet turtle stays small if kept in a small tank.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Turtles keep growing and need a big tank. Always wash your hands after touching one.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Red-eared sliders love to bask under a lamp, just like sunbathing on a rock.

name: Ferret
visual_anchor: A playful cream-and-brown ferret with a masked face poking its head out of a colorful fabric play tunnel, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Long, slinky pet with a masked face
Loves crawling through tunnels and tubes
Sleeps for many hours each day
A close cousin of weasels and otters

facts_and_myths.claim: Ferrets sleep for many hours each day.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ferrets often sleep 14 hours or more, then have bursts of very playful energy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A group of ferrets is called a business.

facts_and_myths.claim: Ferrets are rodents, like hamsters and mice.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ferrets are not rodents. They belong to the weasel family, along with otters and badgers.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Baby ferrets are called kits.

name: Chinchilla
visual_anchor: A super soft gray chinchilla with big round ears and a bushy tail rolling happily in a bowl of fine sand, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small, super soft gray pet rodent
Has big round ears and a bushy tail
Cleans itself by rolling in fine dust
Comes from the high Andes Mountains

facts_and_myths.claim: Chinchillas have some of the thickest fur of any land animal.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Many hairs grow from each tiny spot on their skin, making their fur incredibly soft and dense.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A single chinchilla hair root can grow dozens of hairs at once.

facts_and_myths.claim: Chinchillas need water baths to stay clean.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their thick fur stays damp too long. Chinchillas clean themselves by rolling in special dust instead.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Chinchillas come from the high Andes Mountains in South America.

name: Gerbil
visual_anchor: Two sandy-brown gerbils with long furry tails standing up on their back legs beside a cardboard tunnel in deep bedding, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small pet rodent with a long, furry tail
Loves digging tunnels in deep bedding
Happier living with a gerbil buddy
Comes from the dry deserts of Mongolia

facts_and_myths.claim: Gerbils come from deserts and drink very little water.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Desert life taught gerbils to save water, so they need only small sips each day.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Gerbils thump their back feet on the ground when they are excited or alarmed.

facts_and_myths.claim: It is fine to pick up a gerbil by its tail.
facts_and_myths.explanation: A gerbil's tail is delicate and can get hurt. Scoop gerbils up gently with both hands.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Gerbils are social animals and are happiest living in pairs or small groups.

name: Cockatiel
visual_anchor: A gray cockatiel with a tall yellow head crest and round orange cheek patches perched on a wooden swing in a bright room, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Small gray pet parrot with a pointy head crest
Has a yellow face and round orange cheek patches
Loves whistling tunes
Comes from Australia

facts_and_myths.claim: Cockatiels raise or lower their head crest to show their mood.
facts_and_myths.explanation: A straight-up crest often means curious or surprised, while a relaxed crest means calm.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Many male cockatiels can learn to whistle whole tunes.

facts_and_myths.claim: Cockatiels are just a big kind of budgie.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cockatiels belong to the cockatoo family, not the budgie family.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Cockatiels are the smallest members of the cockatoo family.

name: Dairy Cow
visual_anchor: A friendly black-and-white dairy cow with a pink nose munching grass in a sunny green meadow beside a red barn, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Big farm animal that says 'moo'
Often has black and white patches
Gives us milk for cheese, butter and yogurt
Chews cud and has a stomach with four parts

facts_and_myths.claim: A cow has one stomach divided into four parts.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The four parts help cows break down tough grass, which they bring back up to chew again.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Cows spend many hours each day chewing their cud.

facts_and_myths.claim: Brown cows give chocolate milk.
facts_and_myths.explanation: All cows give white milk. Chocolate milk is made by adding cocoa and sugar.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Every black-and-white cow has its own unique spot pattern, a bit like a fingerprint.

name: Horse
visual_anchor: A glossy chestnut horse with a flowing mane galloping across a green field under a bright blue sky, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Large animal that people ride
Has hooves, a long mane and a swishy tail
Neighs, trots and gallops
Its height is measured in 'hands'

facts_and_myths.claim: Horses can sleep while standing up.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Special joints lock their legs in place so they can doze standing, though they lie down for deep sleep.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Horses have some of the largest eyes of any land mammal.

facts_and_myths.claim: Horses can see directly behind themselves.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Horses have a blind spot right behind them, so never walk close behind a horse.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: One 'hand' used to measure a horse equals four inches.

name: Shetland Pony
visual_anchor: A small, shaggy brown Shetland pony with a thick fluffy mane standing on a windy green island hillside, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Very small, sturdy pony
Has a thick, shaggy coat and bushy mane
Surprisingly strong for its size
Comes from islands off the north of Scotland

facts_and_myths.claim: Shetland ponies are very strong for their small size.
facts_and_myths.explanation: These tough little ponies were used to carry heavy loads and pull carts.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Shetland ponies once worked in coal mines, pulling carts through narrow tunnels.

facts_and_myths.claim: A pony is just a baby horse.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ponies are fully grown small horses. A baby horse or pony is called a foal.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Their thick winter coat keeps them cozy on cold, windy islands.

name: Domestic Donkey
visual_anchor: A gentle gray donkey with long fuzzy ears and a white nose standing in a sunny farmyard beside a wooden fence, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Gray or brown farm animal with very long ears
Makes a loud 'hee-haw' sound
Carries heavy packs on its back
Often has a dark cross-shaped stripe over its shoulders

facts_and_myths.claim: Donkeys make a loud 'hee-haw' sound called a bray.
facts_and_myths.explanation: A donkey's bray is loud and can be heard from far away.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Many donkeys have a dark cross-shaped stripe on their back and shoulders.

facts_and_myths.claim: Donkeys are lazy and stubborn.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Donkeys are careful. They stop to think when something looks unsafe instead of rushing ahead.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Donkeys love having a donkey buddy and can get lonely on their own.

name: Domestic Pig
visual_anchor: A happy pink pig with a curly tail and floppy ears rolling in a cool mud puddle on a sunny farm, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Pink farm animal with a curly tail
Says 'oink' and sniffs with a flat snout
Rolls in mud on hot days
One of the smartest animals on the farm

facts_and_myths.claim: Pigs roll in mud to stay cool.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Pigs cannot sweat much, so cool mud helps them beat the heat and protects their skin from sunburn.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A pig's snout is so sensitive it can sniff out truffles hidden underground.

facts_and_myths.claim: Pigs are dirty animals that love being messy.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Pigs are actually tidy and like to keep their sleeping area clean.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pigs are very smart and can learn tricks, like coming when their name is called.

name: Sheep
visual_anchor: A fluffy white sheep with a soft woolly coat and a little lamb beside it grazing on a green hillside under puffy clouds, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Fluffy farm animal that says 'baa'
Its babies are called lambs
Gives us wool for sweaters and blankets
Likes to stay close to its flock

facts_and_myths.claim: Many sheep need a woolly haircut every year.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their wool keeps growing, so farmers shear them, usually once a year, to keep them comfy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sheep can remember and recognize the faces of other sheep and people.

facts_and_myths.claim: Shearing a sheep hurts it.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Shearing is like a haircut. Done gently, it does not hurt and keeps sheep cool in summer.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sheep have rectangular pupils that help them see almost all the way around.

name: Domestic Goat
visual_anchor: A playful white goat with small horns and a little beard climbing on a rock in a sunny farmyard, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Farm animal that bleats and often has a beard
Loves to climb on rocks and fences
Gives milk used to make tasty cheese
Has rectangular, sideways pupils

facts_and_myths.claim: Goats have rectangular pupils.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their sideways pupils give goats a wide view to spot things around them.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Baby goats are called kids.

facts_and_myths.claim: Goats eat tin cans.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Goats nibble things to explore, but they eat plants, leaves and hay, not cans.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Morocco, some goats climb argan trees to nibble the leaves and fruit.

name: Hen
visual_anchor: A plump reddish-brown hen sitting on a straw nest with a few eggs while fluffy yellow chicks peek out beside her, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Farm bird that clucks and pecks at seeds
Lays eggs in a cozy nest
Has a small red comb on its head
A mother of fluffy chicks

facts_and_myths.claim: A hen can lay eggs without a rooster.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Hens lay eggs on their own. A rooster is only needed for eggs that hatch into chicks.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some chicken breeds lay blue or green eggs.

facts_and_myths.claim: Brown eggs are healthier than white eggs.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Shell color depends on the hen's breed. Inside, brown and white eggs are basically the same.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Mother hens cluck to their chicks even before the chicks hatch.

name: Rooster
visual_anchor: A proud rooster with a big red comb and shiny green-and-orange tail feathers crowing on a fence post at sunrise, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Male chicken with colorful feathers
Has a big red comb and wattles
Crows 'cock-a-doodle-doo'
One of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac

facts_and_myths.claim: Roosters only crow at sunrise.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Roosters crow most in the morning, but they can crow at any time of day.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Roosters do a clucking 'food dance' to call hens over to tasty snacks they find.

facts_and_myths.claim: The rooster is one of the animals of the Chinese zodiac.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The rooster is the tenth of the 12 zodiac animals in the Chinese calendar.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The rooster is a famous national symbol of France.

name: Domestic Duck
visual_anchor: A white farm duck with a bright orange bill leading a line of fluffy yellow ducklings to a sparkling farm pond, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Farm bird that quacks and waddles
Has webbed feet and a flat orange bill
Its fluffy babies follow it in a line
Most are descended from wild mallards

facts_and_myths.claim: Ducklings follow the first moving thing they see after hatching.
facts_and_myths.explanation: This is called imprinting. Ducklings usually follow their mother to stay safe.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Most farm ducks are descended from wild mallard ducks.

facts_and_myths.claim: A duck's quack does not echo.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Scientists tested it, and a duck's quack does echo. It is just hard to hear outdoors.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ducks spread oil from a gland near their tail to keep feathers waterproof.

name: Domestic Turkey
visual_anchor: A big turkey with a fanned-out bronze tail and red wattle strutting proudly through autumn leaves on a farm, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Large farm bird that spreads its tail like a fan
Males make a funny 'gobble' sound
Has a red, fleshy flap hanging over its beak
Its wild ancestors come from North America

facts_and_myths.claim: Male turkeys make a loud 'gobble' sound.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Male turkeys gobble to talk to other turkeys, and they can be heard far away.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The fleshy flap that hangs over a turkey's beak is called a snood.

facts_and_myths.claim: Turkeys come from the country of Turkey.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Turkeys come from North America. Their name came from a mix-up with another bird long ago.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The skin on a turkey's head can change color when it gets excited.

name: Water Buffalo
visual_anchor: A calm dark-gray water buffalo with big curved horns resting in a shallow pond beside bright green rice fields, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Big dark-gray animal with wide curved horns
Loves to soak in mud and water
Helps farmers plow rice fields in Asia
Its milk is used to make mozzarella cheese

facts_and_myths.claim: Water buffalo help farmers plow wet rice fields.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their wide hooves and strong bodies help them walk through muddy rice paddies in Asia.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Real Italian mozzarella is often made from water buffalo milk.

facts_and_myths.claim: Water buffalo are the same animal as the American bison.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Water buffalo come from Asia. American bison are a different animal from North America.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The carabao, a type of water buffalo, is a beloved symbol of the Philippines.

name: Highland Cattle
visual_anchor: A shaggy reddish-orange Highland cow with long curved horns and fluffy bangs over its eyes standing in a misty Scottish glen, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Shaggy cattle with long, fluffy hair
Has long curved horns and bangs over its eyes
Often reddish-orange in color
Comes from the Highlands of Scotland

facts_and_myths.claim: Highland cattle have two layers of hair.
facts_and_myths.explanation: A soft under layer and a long, oily outer layer keep them cozy in cold, rainy weather.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A group of Highland cattle is called a fold instead of a herd.

facts_and_myths.claim: Highland cattle cannot see through their long bangs.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They can see fine. Their bangs protect their eyes from wind, rain and flies.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Highland cattle come in red, black, yellow, white and other colors.

name: Domestic Goose
visual_anchor: A big white farm goose with an orange beak and long neck honking beside a little pond, fluffy goslings nearby, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Large farm bird with a long neck
Honks loudly when strangers come near
Its babies are called goslings
Its soft down fills cozy pillows and jackets

facts_and_myths.claim: Some farms keep geese as noisy guards.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Geese honk loudly at strangers, warning farmers that someone is coming.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A baby goose is called a gosling.

facts_and_myths.claim: Geese have real teeth in their beaks.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Geese have no real teeth. Their beaks have tooth-like ridges for gripping grass.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Geese can even have tooth-like ridges on their tongues.

name: Ox
visual_anchor: Two strong brown oxen joined by a wooden yoke pulling a cart along a dirt road past golden fields, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Big, strong cattle trained to do farm work
Pulls carts and plows, often in pairs
Works with a wooden bar called a yoke
The second animal of the Chinese zodiac

facts_and_myths.claim: Oxen often work in pairs, joined by a wooden yoke.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The yoke links two oxen so they can pull a heavy plow or cart together.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The plural of ox is oxen, not oxes.

facts_and_myths.claim: An ox is a totally different species from a cow.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Oxen are cattle, the same species as cows, that are trained to pull and work.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Ox is the second animal in the Chinese zodiac.

name: Clydesdale Horse
visual_anchor: A huge bay Clydesdale horse with a white face stripe and fluffy white hair around its hooves trotting in a sunny paddock, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Giant, gentle farm horse
Has fluffy white hair around its lower legs
Often bay-brown with a white face stripe
Named after a river valley in Scotland

facts_and_myths.claim: Clydesdales have long, silky hair on their lower legs called feathers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: This fluffy leg hair is one of the easiest ways to recognize a Clydesdale.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Clydesdales are named after the River Clyde area in Scotland.

facts_and_myths.claim: Clydesdales are too big to be gentle.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Clydesdales are famous for being calm and friendly, earning the nickname gentle giants.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A Clydesdale's horseshoe is much bigger than a regular riding horse's shoe.

name: Mule
visual_anchor: A sturdy brown mule with long ears carrying colorful packs along a sunny canyon trail with red rock cliffs, 9:16 vertical shot.
core_traits: Farm animal with long ears and a horse-like body
Carries heavy packs on steep mountain trails
Very sure-footed on rocky paths
Has a horse mom and a donkey dad

facts_and_myths.claim: A mule's mom is a horse and its dad is a donkey.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Mules mix the strength of horses with the careful, tough nature of donkeys.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Mules carry visitors and supplies down the steep trails of the Grand Canyon.

facts_and_myths.claim: Mules are just stubborn donkeys.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Mules are a horse-donkey mix, and they are smart and careful, not simply stubborn.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A mule's long ears come from its donkey dad.
